posts.title: Another warship at the bottom of the sea
posts.description: Not long after taking Putin's beloved bridge to Crimea out of business, the Ukrainians have sunk another of his warships, this time far off on the coast of North Africa. There's no end to the embarrassments that President Zelensky is able to inflict on the Kremlin -- and, for that matter, on the White House. Who now is holding the cards, Mr Trump, or are you still trying to find Libya on the map?

posts.title: Pity about your bridge, Vladimir
posts.description: Twelve years ago, Russia's president-for-life decided to return the Crimean peninsula to Moscow's control. He accomplished this almost overnight by sending his "little green men" -- Russian soldiers in uniform but without any national insignia -- into Crimea and the Donbas region of eastern Ukraine to start another of his frozen wars, in which the comparatively huge Russian army would gradually force its way into national control. As a symbol of who and what really mattered, Putin himself drove a truck over the Kerch Bridge when its twin spans -- one for trains, the other for vehicles -- were complete. Ukraine of course set out to destroy the bridge, which soon became the most thoroughly defended mile or so in Putin's version of the Russian Empire begun by Catherine the Great and solidified by Joseph Stalin on the ruins of the Second World War. But now Ukraine has done it again: sections of both spans now lie at the bottom of the sea, and apparently neither trains nor trucks can travel

posts.title: Viva Maria!
posts.description: The only downside to Maria Corina Machado is that she gave her Nobel Peace Prize to that imbecile in the White House. But now she's back in Venezuela -- and isn't it wonderful how she pronounces that second-last syllable of her homeland? Perhaps Marco Rubio, who seems to be Trump's man in charge of Caracas, can gently guide his boss to embrace Maria rather than the thuggish Delcy Rodriguez as Venezuela's interim leader. And who knows? Perhaps he'd even return that Nobel statuette to its rightful owner....
